answer: Each agent must lock a cryptographic bond at the network vertex where its identity is minted; the bond is tied to a proof‑of‑stake ledger that records every interaction as a leaf in an orchard‑shaped Merkle tree. When a peer detects duplicate signatures or inconsistent state, it submits a challenge to the harbor node, which runs a zero‑knowledge verification; a successful proof of Sybil behaviour triggers an automatic slash of the bond and rebroadcasts the revocation across the mesh.
